# 'milo' Dialect

_Milo's own MLIR dialect: ownership, checks and Vec memory as IR_

Milo compiles through MLIR, and this is its dialect. The Milo compiler type-checks the
source and emits milo dialect IR (`src/emit-mlir.ts`); `milo-opt`, a C++ tool built on
upstream MLIR, runs Milo's passes on it and lowers it to the LLVM dialect.

The dialect exists to keep facts that are lost in LLVM IR:

- Ownership: a slot owns a value with drop glue, and the `milo-elaborate-drops` pass
  decides from the IR where each value is dropped.
- Checks: a bounds check or a checked arithmetic op is a panic point ordered against
  element writes, so `milo-version-bounds-checks` can version a loop instead of hoisting
  the check out of it.
- Vec memory: a Vec's header (ptr, len, cap) and its elements are separate memory, so an
  element store never invalidates a loaded length or data pointer.

Types: ints carry their signedness in the type (si32, ui8), never in an attribute; bool is
i1; `!milo.ref` is a second-class reference (a place that is never stored), `!milo.ptr`
a raw pointer.

Control flow stays structured (milo.if, milo.while, milo.loop, milo.for, milo.match,
milo.scope) until `milo-lower-structured-cf` lowers it to cf branches; break, continue
and return may exit any number of them.

The op verifiers define valid milo IR. A complete program also needs the module the Milo
compiler emits around it (runtime, globals, the main wrapper), so the dialect is not yet a
standalone target for other frontends.

## Operations

### `milo.add` (::milo::AddOp)

_Integer or float addition_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.add` $lhs `,` $rhs (`wrapping` $wrapping^)? attr-dict `:` type($result)
```

`lhs + rhs`. On an int it panics on overflow (in the signedness of the type) unless
`wrapping`, Milo's @wrapping or --no-overflow-checks, which gives two's complement. The
panic names the op's location. Floats never trap and never carry `wrapping`.

Traits: `SameOperandsAndResultType`

Interfaces: `InferTypeOpInterface`, `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

_The address of a place as a raw pointer_

Syntax:

```

### `milo.bits` (::milo::BitsOp)

_A bit intrinsic of an integer_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.bits` $kind `,` $value (`,` $amount^)? attr-dict `:` type($value) (`,` type($amount)^)? `->` type($result)
```

`ctpop`, `ctlz`, `cttz` count bits of `value` (defined for 0: the width) and give an
si64; `bitreverse` gives the value's type; `fshl` / `fshr` rotate `value` by
`amount` (taken mod the width), the value's type.

Traits: `AlwaysSpeculatableImplTrait`

### `milo.bounds_check` (::milo::BoundsCheckOp)

_Panic unless 0 <= index < len_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.bounds_check` $index `,` $len attr-dict `:` type($index) `,` type($len)
```

Panics unless 0 <= index < len (one unsigned compare). Reading VecElems pins it after
every earlier element store: a task that recovers from the panic observes exactly
the writes made before the failing index. The panic names the op's location.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Read on ::milo::VecElemsResource, MemoryEffects::Write on ::milo::PanicResource}`

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `index` | 64-bit signless integer or 64-bit signed integer |
| `len` | 64-bit signless integer or 64-bit signed integer |



### `milo.break` (::milo::BreakOp)

_Leave the innermost loop_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.break` attr-dict
```

Leaves the innermost enclosing milo.while, milo.loop or milo.for, from any depth of
nested regions inside its body (not from a while's cond region). A terminator that is
not a region branch: it jumps over the regions between it and its loop.

Traits: `Terminator`

### `milo.cast` (::milo::CastOp)

_Convert a scalar to another scalar type_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.cast` $operand attr-dict `:` type($operand) `to` type($result)
```

`x as T` between scalars. Never traps. Int to int sign- or zero-extends by the
source's signedness (bool zero-extends), or truncates. Float to int saturates (NaN is

### `milo.ccall` (::milo::CCallOp)

_A call of a C function that is variadic_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.ccall` $callee `(` $args `)` `fixed` $fixed attr-dict `:` functional-type($args, $result)
```

`printf(fmt, ...)`, `open(path, flags, ...)`: the first `fixed` arguments are the
declared ones, the rest go through C's `...` as they are (no promotion, as legacy
codegen passes them). The callee is declared variadic here.

### `milo.check_unaliased` (::milo::CheckUnaliasedOp)

_Panic if two by-ref arguments are the same place_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.check_unaliased` $lhs `,` $rhs attr-dict `:` type($lhs) `,` type($rhs)
```

Before a call with two by-ref arguments of which one is `&mut`: panics if they are the
same place. The checker rejects the aliasing it can prove; this is the runtime half, and
what makes `noalias` on a `&mut` param sound.

### `milo.closure` (::milo::ClosureOp)

_A by-reference closure value_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.closure` $fn (`(` $captures^ `:` type($captures) `)`)? (`heap` $heap^)? (`static` $staticEnv^)? attr-dict `:` type($result)
```

A by-reference closure literal: `fn` is its body, a func.func taking `(!milo.ptr env,
params...)`, and the env (an entry-block slot of this frame: null drop header, then
the captures' addresses in order) lends it every capture in place. The checker keeps
such a closure from outliving the frame; no captures means a null env. Not Pure: the
body may write any capture whenever the value is called.

`heap`: the env is malloc'd instead, its drop header `free` (legacy genClosure's
heapEnv, a scoped task's literal: the creating frame returns before the scope joins
the task, and the task's reap calls the header). It owns the block and no capture.

`static`: the env is a module-level global (`<fn>_env`) instead of a slot: a closure
built by a global's initializer, whose frame is gone before the global is called
(legacy genClosure's staticEnv). Its captures are globals, already static.

Interfaces: `SymbolUserOpInterface`

### `milo.cmp` (::milo::CmpOp)

_Compare two scalars or pointers_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.cmp` $predicate `,` $lhs `,` $rhs attr-dict `:` type($lhs)
```

Signedness comes from the operand type (bool compares as signed i1, as legacy codegen
does). On floats every comparison is ordered except `ne`, which holds when either side
is NaN, so `x != x` is true for NaN.

### `milo.contract_check` (::milo::ContractCheckOp)

_Panic unless a contract clause holds_

Syntax:

```

A `requires`, `ensures` or `invariant` clause checked at run time (a contract-checking

and aborts (legacy emitContractCheck, through the out-of-line __milo_contract_fail).

### `milo.copy` (::milo::CopyOp)

_Copy a struct, enum or array between places_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.copy` $src `,` $dst attr-dict `:` type($src) `,` type($dst) `of` $elem
```

A `T` copied from one place to another, as legacy's llvm.memcpy: how a 128+ byte
aggregate moves between places without becoming an SSA value (SROA splits a whole
aggregate load per element). Either side is a slot (`!milo.ref<T>`) or a raw pointer to a
T. It moves no ownership by itself: an owned source that gives its value up is emptied
right after with an unused milo.move, an owned destination is marked milo.filled.
The same place on both sides (`swap(v[i], v[j])` once CSE merges the two element
references) copies nothing.

### `milo.div` (::milo::DivOp)

_Integer or float division_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.div` $lhs `,` $rhs (`wrapping` $wrapping^)? attr-dict `:` type($result)
```

`lhs / rhs`. An integer divisor of zero always panics, `wrapping` or not; signed
MIN / -1 panics unless `wrapping`, which yields MIN. Signed division truncates toward
zero. Floats follow IEEE and never trap.

Traits: `SameOperandsAndResultType`

### `milo.drop` (::milo::DropOp)

_Run the drop glue of the value in a place_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.drop` $ref (`if` $flag^)? attr-dict `:` type($ref)
```

The value in the slot dies: its drop glue runs (legacy's, codegen mlirDropHelper). On an
owned slot this is "if it holds one" until milo-elaborate-drops decides: it erases the
drop where the slot is empty on every path, keeps it where it is full on every path,
and gives it the slot's drop flag (`if %flag`) where that differs by path. A field of an
owned slot that a milo.move takes a value out of is tracked the same way, and a drop of
a place with such a field under it becomes drops of its fields, the last first. On any
other place (a `&mut` param, a field) it always holds one.

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `ref` | the address of a place: a local slot, a field, an element |
| `flag` | 1-bit signless integer |

### `milo.for` (::milo::ForOp)

_A counted loop over a half-open int range_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.for` $start `to` $end `:` type($start) $bodyRegion attr-dict
```

`for i in start..end { body }`: both bounds evaluated once, before the loop; the body's
entry block argument is `i`, immutable inside the body. `<` follows the signedness of
the type and the step is a plain (wrapping) +1, as legacy codegen emits it: i < end
already bounds i, so the step cannot overflow.

### `milo.match` (::milo::MatchOp)

_A switch on an enum tag or an int or bool_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.match` $subject `:` type($subject) (`->` type($results)^)? $cases (`default` $hasDefault^)? $arms attr-dict
```

`match subject { arms }`, one region per arm. On an enum, `cases` holds each arm's tag
and the arm's entry block takes that variant's payload fields as arguments (what the
pattern binds); on an int or bool, `cases` are the literal values and arms take none.
With `default` the last region is the `_` arm; without one, a value matching no case
is unreachable (the checker proved the match exhaustive). With results it is an
expression: each arm yields them or ends in a jump.

Traits: `RecursiveMemoryEffects`

Interfaces: `RegionBranchOpInterface`

### `milo.panic_if` (::milo::PanicIfOp)

_Panic with a message when a condition holds_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.panic_if` $bad `,` $message (`(` $values^ `)`)? attr-dict
```

When `bad` holds, prints `message` to stderr as a printf format and aborts through the
panic hook. `message` is the whole text, site included, as the emitter builds it; its
only conversions are `%lld`, one per value, at most three. Every other `%` is written
`%%`.

```mlir
milo.panic_if %neg, "milo: negative length at a.milo:3:9: %lld\n"(%n)
```

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Write on ::milo::PanicResource}`

### `milo.replay.enter` (::milo::ReplayEnterOp)

_Enter a record/replay engine function_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.replay.enter` attr-dict
```

Entry to and exit from a record/replay engine function (std/replay; HIRFunction
replayEngine): while the recorder's heap switch is on, the engine's own allocations go
to libc's malloc rather than the recorded fixed-address heap, so their nesting depth is
counted in `replay$rrDepth`. Enter at the top of the body, exit before every return.



### `milo.replay.exit` (::milo::ReplayExitOp)

_Leave a record/replay engine function_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.replay.exit` attr-dict
```

The exit half of milo.replay.enter: decrements `replay$rrDepth` before every return of a
record/replay engine function.

### `milo.sub` (::milo::SubOp)

_Integer or float subtraction_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.sub` $lhs `,` $rhs (`wrapping` $wrapping^)? attr-dict `:` type($result)
```

never trap and never carry `wrapping`.

### `milo.var` (::milo::VarOp)

_A mutable local slot_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `milo.var` $name (`owned` $owned^)? (`structural` $structural^)? attr-dict `:` type($ref)
```

`var name`: a mutable local. Must sit in the function's entry block, so the frame is
fixed: a slot allocated inside a loop would grow the stack every iteration.

`owned`: the slot holds a value with drop glue (a string, a Vec) that it owns. Such a
slot is listed by the milo.scope that owns it; from there on the IR says only where the
value is stored (milo.store), moved out (milo.move) and read in place (milo.load, a view
that never owns), and milo-scope-drops / milo-elaborate-drops decide where it dies.

`structural`: an owned slot holding a structural clone (legacy emitDeepCloneFromPtr of a
Vec element matched by value), which shares any resource handle with the original: its
drop is legacy's structural one (`milo.sdrop.<key>`), which runs no user Drop.

#### Attributes:

<tr><td><code>structural</code></td><td>::mlir::UnitAttr</td><td>unit attribute</td></tr>
</table>

| :----: | ----------- |
| `ref` | the address of a place: a local slot, a field, an element |

_Move the next element out of a vectail_

## Types

### ArrayTailType

_A fixed array being consumed from the front_

Syntax:

```
!milo.arraytail<
  ::mlir::Type   # arrayType
>
```

What is left of a fixed array a consuming `for x in [a, b]` takes apart from the front:
legacy's `{ [N x T], i64 cursor }` (genConsumedIterable). As !milo.vectail: the drop
glue drops the elements from the cursor on, so a break or a return out of the loop drops
exactly what no iteration took. Lives only in an owned slot, never as an SSA value.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| arrayType | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### ArrayType

_A fixed-size array, held only in places_

Syntax:

```
!milo.array<
  ::mlir::Type,   # elementType
  int64_t   # size
>
```

A fixed-size array `[T; N]`, legacy's `[N x T]`. Held only in places, as a 128+ byte
aggregate is, whatever its size: an SSA value exists only at the ABI (a by-value param
or argument), so a large buffer is never split per element. Its elements own nothing.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elementType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
| size | `int64_t` |  |

### DynRefType

_A borrowed interface value_

Syntax:

```
!milo.dynref<
  ::llvm::StringRef   # iface
>
```

A `&I`: legacy's literal `{ ptr data, ptr itable }`, borrowing both (a param, a
`&T` or `&mut T` coerced to `&I`). It owns nothing; a method
call through it is legacy's dispatch in a helper, as for `!milo.dyn`.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| iface | `::llvm::StringRef` |  |

### DynType

_An owned box of an interface value_

Syntax:

```
!milo.dyn<
  ::llvm::StringRef   # iface
>
```

A `Heap<I>` of an interface: legacy's `{ ptr data, ptr itable }`, owned (its drop glue,
legacy's `milo.drop.dyn.<I>`, runs the concrete type's drop through the itable and frees
the box). Opaque: a method call through it is legacy's dispatch in a helper.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| iface | `::llvm::StringRef` |  |

### EnumType

_A tagged enum by value, with its layout_

A tagged enum by value, with the layout legacy codegen computed (EnumLayout), spelled
out so nothing here recomputes it: `size` bytes stored as `[size/align x i(8*align)]`
(or `{ i32 }` when size is 0, a fieldless enum), the i32 tag in bytes 0..4, and each
variant's fields at the byte offsets after `at`:
  !milo.enum<"Shape", size = 24, align = 8, [0: (f64 at 8), 1: (f64 at 8, f64 at 16), 2: ()]>
A niche-packed enum (EnumLayout.niche: two variants, one fieldless, one with a single
field) has no tag word. It is stored as its payload alone, `{ P }`, and the fieldless
variant is the value after `niche` in the payload's leading integer:
  !milo.enum<"Option_R", niche = 2147483647 : i32, [0: (si32 at 0), 1: ()]>

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| name | `::llvm::StringRef` |  |

### FnType

_A fn value: fn pointer and env_

A fn value `(T) => R`: legacy's `{ ptr fn, ptr env }`. The fn takes the env first, then
the params of `signature` (a `&T` param is a !milo.ref, a `&Vec<T>` a !milo.vec). A
plain one's env is null or a frame's (milo.closure), never owned, so the value is Copy
and has no drop glue. An `owning` one (`move (T) => R`, `!milo.fn<owning (T) -> R>`)
holds a heap env whose first word is its drop glue: it is an owned value, dropped
through legacy's glue for owning closures (milo.drop.ownfn).

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| signature | `::mlir::FunctionType` |  |
| owning | `bool` |  |

### HeapType

_An owned box holding one value_

Syntax:

```
!milo.heap<
  ::mlir::Type   # valueType
>
```

A `Heap<T>`: legacy's malloc'd pointer to one T, owned (its drop glue, legacy's
`milo.drop.heap.<t>`, drops the T and frees the box). `*h` is the place milo.heap.place
gives. Through it a type can hold itself (`enum Expr { Add(Heap<Expr>, ...) }`).

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| valueType | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### MapType

_A HashMap value_

Syntax:

```
!milo.map<
  ::mlir::Type,   # keyType
  ::mlir::Type   # valueType
>
```

A `HashMap<K, V>` value: legacy's `%HashMap = { ptr data, i64 len, i64 cap, i64 seed,
i64 tombs }` (codegen-map.ts). Its methods are Milo code in std/hashmap that reads it
through a raw pointer, so no op here looks inside; K and V only name its drop glue
(legacy's, `milo.drop.map.<k>.<v>`).

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| keyType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
| valueType | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### PtrType

_A raw pointer, untyped_

Syntax: `!milo.ptr`

A raw pointer `*T` (unsafe code only). Untyped, like LLVM's: `*T` can be reinterpreted,
so the pointee type rides on each access (milo.ptr.load/store), not on the pointer.
Unlike a !milo.ref it is a first-class value: stored, returned, compared, cast.


### RefType

_The address of a place: a local slot, a field, an element_

Syntax:

```
!milo.ref<
  ::mlir::Type   # pointee
>
```

The address of a place holding a `pointee`: a mutable local (milo.var), a field, an
element, a global or a by-ref param (Mojo's !lit.ref, ClangIR's !cir.ptr).
Second-class, as Milo's references are: it never escapes a call, is never stored and
never returned (milo-verify checks this). Its memory is the Slot resource, disjoint
from Vec headers and elements; a place reached through a raw pointer is a !milo.ptr.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| pointee | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### StringType

_Milo's string value_

Syntax: `!milo.string`

Milo's `string` value: legacy's `%String = { ptr data, i64 len, i64 cap }`, the same
bytes on both sides of the splice. A literal has cap 0: its buffer is static, so its
drop glue does nothing. Strings and Vecs are owned values: see milo.var `owned`.


### StructType

_A struct by value, identified by name_

A struct by value, named as legacy codegen names its LLVM type (`%Point`), with its
fields' types in declaration order: `!milo.struct<"Point", si64, f64>`. It lowers to
the identified LLVM struct of that name, so a spliced body uses the module's own
definition and the layout is LLVM's natural one, which is legacy's.
A type with its own `impl Drop` says so after its name, `!milo.struct<"Noisy" drop, si64>`
(enums the same way): it has drop glue whatever its fields are, and the glue runs the
user's drop first (legacy's, through `milo.drop.<key>`).
Structs and enums are identified by name, as LLVM's identified structs are: the body is
set once, after the type exists, so a type can hold itself through a Vec (a JSON value,
a tree). Inside its own body it is spelled by name alone, `!milo.enum<"Json">`, which is
the same type. A second body for a name must equal the first (the parser checks).

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| name | `::llvm::StringRef` |  |

### VecTailType

_A Vec being consumed from the front_

Syntax:

```
!milo.vectail<
  ::mlir::Type   # elementType
>
```

What is left of a Vec a consuming `for x in makeVec()` takes apart from the front:
legacy's `{ %Vec, i64 cursor }` (genConsumedIterable). The elements before the cursor
were moved out; the drop glue drops those from the cursor on, then frees the buffer, so
a break or a return out of the loop frees exactly what no iteration took. Lives only in
an owned slot (milo.vectail.init), never as an SSA value.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elementType | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### VecType

_A Vec by reference: the address of its header_

Syntax:

```
!milo.vec<
  ::mlir::Type   # elementType
>
```

A `Vec<T>` passed by reference: the address of its {ptr, len, cap} header (a `&Vec<T>`
or `&mut Vec<T>` param, or milo.vec.place of a slot). Borrowed: it owns nothing, and
nothing drops through it. The indexing and len ops take it.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elementType | `::mlir::Type` |  |

### VecValType

_A Vec value, the header itself_

Syntax:

```
!milo.vecval<
  ::mlir::Type   # elementType
>
```

A `Vec<T>` value: legacy's `%Vec = { ptr data, i64 len, i64 cap }`. Its place, the address
of that header, is `!milo.vec<T>` (milo.vec.place), which the indexing ops take.

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elementType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
